description: We build factory panelized wall systems for houses. To save material we want to frame load-bearing exterior walls of two-storey homes with 2x4 studs at 600 mm centres supporting the second floor and roof, with a structural header system of our own design. Our in-house tables say it works. What does Alberta need from us?
known_facts: 2x4 studs at 600 mm on centre, load-bearing

missing_info.field: unsupported stud height and complete load path including the proprietary header
missing_info.why: Establish the table comparison and the scope of the proposed structural design.

missing_info.field: structural design basis and responsible designer
missing_info.why: Part 9 permits listed prescriptive, good-engineering-practice and Part 4 routes; departing from one table does not alone establish the chosen route.

should_cite.why: Candidate benchmark only; deciding facts must be obtained first.
Part 9 structural members may instead be designed by engineering (acceptable-solution fork)

gold.engineering_reason: The Part 4 route requires a registered professional; the selected design basis and any AHJ special-safety requirement remain unresolved for the proposed houses.
